wars.note: The two pages give different treaties (Meaux-Paris 1229 on the Crown page, Corbeil 1258 on the James I page); the outcome of Muret itself is not on the Crown page.

wars.name: War of the Sicilian Vespers

zones.text: the island of Sicily, fought over by Aragon, Anjou and, from 1296, Frederick III

wars.outcome: Peter III was crowned in Palermo in 1282; the crowns divided on 2 November 1285 and reunited in 1291; the Treaty of Anagni of 1295 forfeited Sicily to the papacy; Frederick III was crowned in March 1296; 'The war ended in 1302 in the Peace of Caltabellotta': Sicily 'became an independent kingdom under the House of Barcelona' and Naples stayed with the House of Anjou.
wars.note: Infobox 30 March 1282 to 31 August 1302. No contest event is given for 1297-1302: the page has James II agreeing in March 1297 to 'make war on his brother' and the fleet at Naples in 1298 but dates no ground taken in Sicily.

wars.name: Aragonese Crusade
wars.outcome: 'Pope Martin IV declared a crusade against Aragon' and France intervened in Iberia; Roger of Lauria beat the French fleet at Les Formigues (3 September, in the 1285 campaign); Peter III died on 2 November 1285. No Cliopatria shape changes.
wars.note: The page has the French invasion reaching Catalonia and Roussillon but gives no territorial result.

wars.name: Aragonese conquest of Majorca (1286)

zones.text: the Balearic Islands of the Kingdom of Majorca

wars.outcome: Alfonso 'invaded the realm of his uncle and conquered the island of Mallorca in 1286'; 'Some 10 years later, a new treaty - the Treaty of Anagni - ordered the return of the islands'.
wars.note: The Majorca page gives no date for Menorca or for the actual return of the islands (the Cliopatria Crown shape keeps them in 1294-1304).

wars.name: Aragonese conquest of Sardinia

zones.text: Cagliari, Gallura and Sassari, then the rest of the Pisan and Genoese land

wars.outcome: James II, allied with Hugh II of Arborea from 1323, took Cagliari, Gallura and Sassari in about a year; 'its de facto existence began in 1324'.
wars.note: The page does not give the 1326 Pisan cession, which is where Cliopatria starts the Sardinian land.

wars.name: Arborean–Aragonese wars

zones.text: the island of Sardinia, Arborean from 1368 except Cagliari and Alghero

wars.outcome: Arborea attacked in 1353 and by 1368 left the Aragonese the port cities of Cagliari and Alghero; 'A peace treaty returned the Aragonese their previous possessions in 1388'; the Arborean army was beaten at Sanluri in 1409; in 1420 the remaining rights were bought for 100,000 gold florins and the kingdom 'extended throughout the island, except for the city of Castelsardo'.
wars.note: The page's own dates disagree (1368 and 1382 for the Arborean successes; a footnote has the two-city kingdom from 1368 to 1388 and 1392 to 1409). Cliopatria draws the loss in 1375 and the recovery in 1422.

wars.name: Conquest of the Kingdom of Majorca by Peter IV

zones.text: the Balearic Islands, Roussillon and Cerdanya

wars.outcome: Peter IV declared James III a contumacious vassal in February 1343, invaded the Balearic Islands in May 1343, took the counties of Roussillon and Cerdanya in 1344 and brought the kingdom 'under the Crown of Aragon'; James III was 'defeated and killed at the Battle of Llucmajor on 25 October 1349'.
wars.note: The Peter IV page (Santa Ponça, 'In March, Peter had declared his realm incorporated', undated) is the second source.

wars.name: War of the Two Peters

zones.text: Aragonese and Valencian land held by Castile in 1363: Tarazona, Alicante, Caudete, Elda, Gandia, Cariñena, Teruel, Segorbe, Morvedre

wars.outcome: Castile took Tarazona on 9 March 1357; the peace of Terrer of 18 May 1361 returned all conquests; in 1363 Castile again occupied Tarazona and entered the Kingdom of Valencia; the peace of Morvedre of 2 July 1363 was not ratified; Peter of Castile was overthrown in 1369; the war 'ended in 1375 with the Treaty of Almazan, without a winner'.
wars.note: The page covers 1356-1369 only; the 1375 treaty is the Peter IV page's. Places such as Teruel 'fell to the Castilians' without a year. Navarre's alliance with Castile (June 1362, Soria) is the page's.

wars.name: Aragonese conquest of the Kingdom of Naples

zones.text: Naples and its district, besieged from 10 November 1441

wars.outcome: The siege of Naples ran 'from 10 November 1441 ... to 2 June the following year'; Alfonso became King of Naples on 2 June 1442 and entered the city on 26 February 1443; he 'reunited under his dominion the kingdoms of Naples and Sicily'.
wars.note: The earlier war (Joanna II's adoption of Alfonso in 1421, the break of 1423-1424, her death in February 1435) is on the page but its campaigns are not dated; the Crown page gives 'added finally in 1442'.

wars.name: Franco-Aragonese dispute over Roussillon and Cerdagne

zones.text: Roussillon and Cerdagne, pledged and seized

wars.outcome: The counties were pledged for a loan of 300,000 crowns and 'seized by France in 1462 when the loan was not repaid'; 'The Treaty of Barcelona was signed on 19 January 1493' and returned them to the Crown.
wars.note: The John II page has the counties pawned to Louis XI (undated) and the Catalan revolt 'pacified in 1472'; neither the Treaty of Bayonne nor the 1463 occupation is on any page opened.

wars.name: Partition and war of Naples

zones.text: the northern kingdom, Abruzzo and Terra di Lavoro

wars.outcome: The Treaty of Granada of 11 November 1500 gave Ferdinand 'the southern areas, notably Calabria' and Louis the north; 'In late 1502 ... full-scale war' followed and 'by the end of 1503 ... Ferdinand took control of the whole kingdom'.
wars.note: Cerignola, Garigliano and the Treaty of Lyon (1504) are not on the page; the Crown page gives 'Conquest of the Kingdom of Naples: 1501–1504'.

certainty.note: The Reconquista frontier with the Almohads and the taifas was a moving march; only the Pyrenean and Navarrese lines and the islands' coasts are firm. The Treaty of Sangüesa (1168) and of Cazorla (1179) divided zones of conquest, not drawn lines.

The Almizra line (1244) fixes the southern frontier with Castile; the islands have coasts. Soft: the Pyrenean frontier of Roussillon and Cerdanya, and the Sardinian conquest of 1324-1326, whose Genoese and Pisan lands the pages do not list.
The Castilian occupation of 1363-1375 and the Arborean front in Sardinia have no drawn line.

Treaty lines (Barcelona 1493, Granada 1500) and coasts; soft: the Arborean front in Sardinia to 1420 (the Greek duchies are catalan-company's and Navarre is drawn by kingdom-of-navarre, neither by this dossier).

IDENTITY AND SPAN. Cliopatria's row runs 1169-1515; this dossier starts in 1162 ('Aragon–Barcelona Union: 1162'; the Alfonso II page has his reign from 18 July 1164, the Crown page 'originated in 1137') because the County of Barcelona dossier of this group ends the county in 1162 and asks this one to carry the land from 1163. For 1163-1168 Cliopatria keeps the Kingdom of Aragon and County of Barcelona as separate rows; the new keyframe crown-of-aragon_1163 is their union, so the kingdom-of-aragon dossier (another part of eu-12) should end in 1162 or its shapes will be drawn twice. The dossier ends with Cliopatria's last shape (1515) and a dissolve into kingdom-of-spain (Cliopatria 1516); the Crown page has the institution lasting to the Nueva Planta decrees of 1715 ('abolished between 1707 and 1716'). The ruler strip (added in the repair) is read from the List of Aragonese monarchs page. Capitals Zaragoza and Barcelona are overlapping entries (the infobox says 'See Capital below').
HOW THE CLIOPATRIA SHAPES WERE TREATED. All 35 shapes have a verdict (1 ok, 33 adjust, 1 wrong) and 18 new keyframes were added; most adjusts change only the years or remove cells of the Greek duchies. The reasons, by period: (1) 1169-1235: Cliopatria's County of Berga row holds Cerdanya (20 cells from 1169) and Roussillon (19 more cells from 1188). The Alfonso II and Roussillon pages put Cerdanya (1168) and Roussillon (1172) with the Crown until Peter II 'granted around 1209' Roussillon to his uncle Sancho, whose son Nuño Sanç died in 1242, but county-of-berga holds Cerdanya continuously from 1162 to 1242, so after the repair Cerdanya (20 cells) is a vassal tint from 1168 (Sancho I), Roussillon (19 cells) is the Crown's own from 1172 and a vassal tint from about 1209 to 1242, and only Berga and the Berguedà (4 cells) are the Crown's own from 1199. (2) 1229-1235: Majorca (31 December 1229) and Ibiza (1235) come before Cliopatria's 1236; Menorca is a Muslim tributary state from 1232 to its conquest on 17 January 1287 (not a gain). (3) 1276-1344: the Kingdom of Majorca is a vassal from 1279, occupied 1286-1295, a vassal again to 1343, and is not the Crown's own land; Cliopatria draws the Balearics in the Crown in 1294-1304 and Sicily to 1304, but Sicily was separate under James II 1285-1290 and left the Crown at Anagni in 1295. (4) 1363-1458: the cells in central Greece belong to the Catalan duchies (Sicilian suzerainty from 1312; the Crown's title 1379-1388/1390), not to the Crown, and are removed throughout: catalan-company (eu-05) draws them as its own land and the Crown is their overlord from 1379 to 1388/1390 (vassal pairs); Corsica (1375-1384) was never conquered. (5) 1442-1458 and 1500-1504: Naples comes six years before Cliopatria's 1450 and four before 1507.
NOT RESOLVED. (a) Provence: Alfonso II was count 'from 1166 until 1173' in the page's text and 1166-1171 in its infobox; Cliopatria never draws it and no keyframe includes it; a gap-filler could add a 1166-1173 keyframe (region 'Provence') and the matching gain/loss events (counterpart county-of-provence, which has no row in polities.csv). (b) Béarn and Bigorre 'paid homage to him in 1187' (Alfonso II page) but no page gives the end, so no vassal pair is written. (c) Occitania: Muret (12 September 1213), Meaux-Paris (1229 on the Crown page), Corbeil (May 1258 on the James I page) are in wars with no zone. (d) Sicily from 1385 and the union with Aragon (Martin I, 1410, 'In 1410, King Martin I died' on the Crown page) and the Compromise of Caspe: no page opened dates the union, so the 1385 gain is confidence 1. (e) Navarre is not drawn by this dossier. John II was King of Navarre jure uxoris from 1425 (with Blanche I) and in possession for life from 1441; he became King of Aragon on 27 June 1458 and died on 20 January 1479 ('Succeeded by Eleanor'), so the two crowns were in personal union 1458-1479 only; the kingdom-of-navarre dossier draws the kingdom throughout and renames it to the Foix line in 1479. (f) Corsica 1422-1449 rests on 'much of Corsica by the 1420s' only. (g) Small Cliopatria moves of 1-2 cells at the frontier (1177, 1188, 1236, 1285, 1294, 1305, 1497, 1502) are not given events; the 1305 swap and the 1285 gain have confidence-1 events. (h) The Murcia/Alicante frontier of 1296-1305 (Torrellas, Elche), Peñíscola/Morella/Burriana, Játiva and Dénia, Pallars Jussà (1192), the Treaty of Lyon (1504), the 1326 Pisan cession, the Treaty of Almazán's terms: none is on a page opened. (i) Pages that failed: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian_War_of_1499%E2%80%931504 and https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian_War_of_1501%E2%80%931504 (not found; the Treaty of Granada (1500) page was used instead).
